cases.statement: Seven rows from two papers, probably one family. 30402268 (Finland) reports index II-1 (woman), relative II-4, daughter III-1 (carriers) and the index's mother I-2 (obligate carrier, not tested; died at 46). 39167656 Family-4 lists index case, brother and daughter with the same variant; Timo Hautala is an author on both. Heterozygous in 30402268; zygosity not stated per person in 39167656.

people.label: II-1
people.key_phenotypes: index patient; autoimmune thyroiditis; psoriasis; articular symptoms; atrophic gastritis; severe inflammatory lung reaction; anaemia; repeated genital HSV infections

quotes.quote: Exome sequencing of the index patient (II-1) identified a novel nonsense mutation in the exon 2 of the TNFAIP3 gene: c.A271T: p.(Lys91*) (ENSG00000118503:ENST00000433680) (figure 1A,B).
The index patient suffered from psoriasis, articular symptoms, atrophic gastritis, severe inflammatory lung reaction, anaemia and repeated genital HSV infections.
The clinical manifestations of the carriers included autoimmune thyroiditis, which was diagnosed in all carriers (I-2, II-1, II-4, III-1) at an early age.

Here we studied patients with HA20 caused by a novel heterozygous TNFAIP3 p.(Lys91*) mutation resulting in severe truncation and production of an N-terminal protein fragment with highly limited functional capacity.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Person-level: early-onset autoimmune thyroiditis in all carriers, with psoriasis, arthritis, gastritis, lung inflammation and infections in the index and polyarticular JIA in the daughter. The authors call the combination unusual. Exome sequencing of the index was filtered for rare heterozygous variants; whether other candidate genes were excluded is not stated.

quotes.quote: The patients exhibit an unusual combination of early-onset autoimmune diseases, autoinflammatory symptoms and immunodeficiency, reflecting the widespread functions of A20 in controlling inflammation.
We searched for rare heterozygous variants, according to the inferred autosomal-dominant inheritance pattern (figure 1A).
The clinical manifestations of the carriers included autoimmune thyroiditis, which was diagnosed in all carriers (I-2, II-1, II-4, III-1) at an early age.

segregation.statement: 30402268: variant found in the index (II-1) and two other affected relatives (II-4, III-1); the index's mother I-2 (affected, deceased) is an obligate carrier, not tested. Unaffected relatives tested: not reported. 39167656 lists three carriers (index, brother, daughter) in Family-4, probably the same family.

functional.statement: Construct and patient-cell assays (30402268). Construct: in HEK293/Flp-In 293 T-REx cells, WT A20 dose-dependently inhibited TNF-α-induced NF-kB reporter activity whereas p.(Lys91*) did not; the mutant was detected only with an N-terminal tag; AP-MS showed loss of several protein interactions. Patient cells: PBMCs of II-1 and III-1 secreted more IL-1β and IL-18 than sex- and age-matched controls; caspase-8 inhibition reduced this.

quotes.quote: The wt A20 dose-dependently inhibited TNF-α induced NF-κB pathway activation, whereas the p.(Lys91*) mutant failed to do so, clearly suggesting a haploinsufficiency (figure 2C).

These analyses revealed that the p.(Lys91*) mutant completely loses physical interactions with BRCC3, TRAD1, WRIP1, TRAF2, BIRC2, F175B, USP9X and HUWE1, with several additional weakened interactions (figure 2D).

We found elevated secretion of IL-1β and IL-18 in PBMCs of the TNFAIP3 p.(Lys91*) carriers in response to LPS +ATP-induced ‘canonical’ (figure 4A,B; left panels) as well as LPS-induced ‘alternative’ pathway of NLRP3 inflammasome activation (figure 4A,B; right panels).
PBMCs from TNFAIP3 p.(Lys91*) mutation carriers, patients 1 (II-1, woman, 30 years) and 2 (III-1, female, 8 years), were compared with sex-matched and age-matched controls 1 and 2, respectively.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Nonsense change, predicted p.(Lys91Ter) per the batch HGVS; 30402268 says it truncates the protein before the OTU domain. Disease mechanism stated as haploinsufficiency / loss of function.

quotes.quote: Here we studied patients with HA20 caused by a novel heterozygous TNFAIP3 p.(Lys91*) mutation resulting in severe truncation and production of an N-terminal protein fragment with highly limited functional capacity.
Haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20) is a severe childhood-onset inflammatory disease characterized by heterozygous germline loss-of-function (LOF) mutations in TNFAIP3 (1, 2).

population_data_in_papers.statement: 30402268 states the variant is not listed in gnomAD; exome filtering discarded variants with frequency >0.01.

quotes.quote: The mutation is not listed in Genome Aggregation Database (gnomAD, Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA) and was predicted to be pathogenic according to the ACMG Standards and Guidelines.
All the common (frequencies >0.01 in the general population) and non-coding variants were discarded.

authors_classification.statement: Authors' own wording is quoted (30402268 refers to the ACMG framework without listing criteria).

quotes.quote: The mutation is not listed in Genome Aggregation Database (gnomAD, Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA) and was predicted to be pathogenic according to the ACMG Standards and Guidelines.
We describe here a family with polyautoimmunity and autoinflammatory symptoms caused by a novel heterozygous TNFAIP3 p.(Lys91*) loss-of-function mutation resulting in haploinsufficiency.

concerns: Same family reported twice: 30402268 (II-1 index, II-4, III-1 daughter) and 39167656 Family-4 (index case, brother, daughter) are probably the same people (same variant, same family structure, shared author Timo Hautala). Likely matches: HA20-ID0035 = HA20-ID0317 (index), HA20-ID0037 = HA20-ID0319 (daughter), HA20-ID0036 = HA20-ID0318 (II-4 = brother; 30402268 does not state II-4's sex). Count the family once.
39167656 writes the protein as p.Lys91fs* (frameshift notation) for a single-nucleotide substitution that 30402268 and the batch describe as a stop codon (p.(Lys91*)).
30402268 uses Ensembl transcript ENST00000433680 and the legacy form c.A271T, not the batch transcript NM_001270508.2.
I-2 is an untested obligate carrier, not a genotyped carrier.
39167656 gives no phenotypes for its Family-4 members beyond inclusion in a table of patients with HA20.
notes_for_panel: One family, two reports. Strongest evidence is 30402268: three genotyped affected carriers, an obligate carrier, a construct reporter assay and patient-cell cytokine studies.
